There’s gonna be a lot of pretty great monsters in the batch. I feel like I’m honing in on my glazing techniques and my construction is getting better and better. Sometimes I wonder if I’m stagnating because I’m working with in certain parameters, but also I feel like in terms of craftsmanship I’m growing. I’m really starting to realize how much you gain by repeatedly doing the same motions and repeatedly using the same general concepts… making these monsters has been such a great Zen like practice. I’ve never really appreciated or understood production pottery or how you could make the same bowl or the same mug, and while this isn’t really that I am using some of the same building techniques the basic thing stays the same, and then it’s really just variables that create these characters, and I’m kind of enjoying the practice of it. #vermontartist #ceramics #scarymonster #kilnreveal

pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

In a few hours’ time I’ll be sending out my newsletter that contains the preview and price-list for this latest collection of pots, (the shop itself goes live tomorrow, 22 November at 7:00 pm GMT), this means there’s still time to sign up to my mailing list if you’d like to receive it. Otherwise, here’s a quick once over of all the pots I’ll be including. There’s a lot this time around, 376 in total, many sold individually, others grouped up in small collections. I always try to aim for a varied mix of vessels, so expect mugs, bowls, teapots, jars, urns, vases and a few other oddities. One thing I’ve particularly enjoyed doing is looking through my growing archive of older pots for pieces to include in these restocks, these are pieces I’ve hung onto for one reason or another, the thing is, you can only do that for so long before too many accumulate and suddenly you find yourself needed the space they once occupied. I’ve also included a few “test” pieces, experiments in black mainly, these are pots from my ongoing search for a reliable black clay body that I can reduction fire to cone ten without too much warping. The examples included in this update are slightly skew-whiff, one even had to have it’s makers mark ground away as it stuck to a kiln shelf, but don’t worry, it’ll come with a certificate to authenticate I made it. If you have any questions about my restock tomorrow, please don’t hesitate to ask, but I’d also recommend reading either the pinned post on my profile, “How my online shop works”, or you can find a much more detailed page on my website, titled “Shop information”. Thanks as always, I can’t wait to share everything with you soon! #pottery #ceramics #handmade #asmr #oddlysatisfying

the stress of making a decent vase 🥵 1. have a plan -sketch or print it out. it’s easy to get lost in the shape trying to figure out where the belly should be how far the base should come out, how broad the shoulders are omgg 2. center tall - this doesn’t mean for all pieces. this usually helps me for 3 ish pounds and up 3. leave the top - this helps especially if you’re narrowing the neck. throw the top after shaping the body and leaving it a little thicker gives you more options 4. how to shape - I couldn’t fit everything I wanted to say in this video. make sure you’re shaping bottom to top. some people (and sometimes me) use ribs the entire time they shape on the inside and out. do what feels best. this is just one way to do it.  5. practice. be better than the rest of us. practice makes progress hope this helps :) #pottery #ceramics #ceramica #funny #vase
